newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end mixed in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end mixed in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Delhi share prices drifted marginally lower in directionless trade on Monday amid selective selling as major investors stayed on the sidelines, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 1.58 points lower at 764.52.
Brokers said the ruling coalition's failure on Sunday to decide whether to raise the prices of some petroleum products induced some investors to adopt a wait-and-watch attitude.
On Sunday, resistance by left-wing parties prevented the ruling United Front from reaching a consensus on how to plug a burgeoning oil-subsidy bill.
"In the absence of any positive developments, the market continued to remain directionless," said Vijay Aggarwal of brokers Mass Financial Services.
Traders said dealing was largely confined to companies that were soon to announce their annual results or the ones that had already announced.
TISCO dropped 4.15 rupees to 169.10 on speculative selling following lower-than-expected results, they said.

Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO), India's largest private steel maker, said after trade closed on Friday that net profit fell to 4.69 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) from 5.66 billion in the previous year.
Reliance Industries slipped 1.00 rupee to 288.90 on foreign selling, brokers said.
ACC fell 81.00 rupees to 1,039.00 on market expectations that the company was unlikely to announce encouraging results for 1996/97 (April-March), brokers said.
State Bank of India rose 4.15 rupees to 304.60.
